_doc: Raspberry Pi Pico (the base model: RP2040, micro-USB), and the cable that plugs into it. kind as in x1c.json.
name: pico

length.source: Raspberry Pi Pico datasheet, 2. Mechanical specification, https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/pico/pico-datasheet.pdf

width.source: Raspberry Pi Pico datasheet, 2. Mechanical specification

pcb.source: Raspberry Pi Pico datasheet: a 1 mm thick PCB

usb_overhang.rule: The micro-USB socket overhangs the board's top edge (the datasheet says it does, in a drawing)
usb_overhang.source: Estimate from the datasheet's Figure 3: measure your Pico

usb_width.source: Common micro-USB B receptacles (about 7.5 mm wide)

usb_height.rule: Micro-USB socket height above the board, rounded up
usb_height.source: Estimate: common micro-USB B receptacles are 2.5 to 3 mm tall; measure your Pico

usb_depth.rule: Micro-USB socket length, front to back

plug_width.rule: A micro-USB cable's plug housing is about this wide: the case opening must let it in
plug_width.source: Estimate: micro-USB plug housings are typically 10 to 11 mm wide; measure your cable

plug_height.rule: A micro-USB cable's plug housing is about this tall
plug_height.source: Estimate: typical housings are 6 to 8 mm tall; measure your cable

pin_pitch.rule: The 40 main pins are on a 0.1 in grid
pin_pitch.source: Raspberry Pi Pico datasheet (RP-008307-DS, release 21, 2026-07-03), 2. Mechanical specification, https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/pico/pico-datasheet.pdf

pin_rows.rule: Between the two rows of pins: one 0.1 in pitch wider than a standard 40-pin DIP (0.6 in), so 0.7 in
pin_rows.source: Raspberry Pi Pico datasheet (RP-008307-DS, release 21, 2026-07-03), 2. Mechanical specification, https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/pico/pico-datasheet.pdf

pin_hole.rule: The Pico's pin holes are 1 mm; a host board's holes for its header pins match
pin_hole.source: Raspberry Pi Pico datasheet (RP-008307-DS, release 21, 2026-07-03), 2. Mechanical specification, https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/pico/pico-datasheet.pdf

pin_pad.rule: Copper pad around each header pin hole on the host board: the 1 mm hole plus a 0.35 mm ring
pin_pad.source: KiCad's 0.1 in pin headers use a 1.0 mm drill and a 1.7 mm pad (Connector_PinHeader_2.54mm)

mount_hole.source: Raspberry Pi Pico datasheet (RP-008307-DS, release 21, 2026-07-03), 2. Mechanical specification, https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/pico/pico-datasheet.pdf

gpio_left.rule: Pins 1 to 20 run down the left edge (USB at the top, seen from above); value: how many carry GPIO, listed in pins, the rest (3, 8, 13, 18) are ground
gpio_left.source: The Pico pinout (datasheet Figure 2, an image); ground pins and pins 30 to 40 confirmed in the datasheet's text. Check against your Pico's silkscreen

gpio_right.rule: Pins 21 to 40 run up the right edge; value: how many carry GPIO, listed in pins (23, 28, 38 ground; 30 RUN, 33 AGND, 35 ADC_VREF, 36 3V3, 37 3V3_EN, 39 VSYS, 40 VBUS)
gpio_right.source: As gpio_left; pins 30, 33 and 35 to 40 are named in the datasheet's text

other_pins.rule: The pins that aren't GPIO, listed in pins: ground, power, run and the ADC reference
other_pins.source: Raspberry Pi Pico datasheet (RP-008307-DS, release 21), 2.1. Raspberry Pi Pico pinout: PIN40 VBUS, PIN39 VSYS, PIN37 3V3_EN, PIN36 3V3, PIN35 ADC_VREF, PIN33 AGND, PIN30 RUN; ground pins as gpio_left and gpio_right

header_spacer.rule: The plastic body of a 0.1 in pin header: a Pico on headers stands this far off the board it's soldered to
header_spacer.source: Standard 2.54 mm pitch male headers have a 2.5 mm tall plastic body (e.g. KiCad's Connector_PinHeader_2.54mm models)
